title: Dinero
blurb: Cómo funciona el dinero, presupuestos, interés compuesto y nociones básicas de inversión.

lessons.title: Cómo funciona el dinero
lessons.summary: Qué es el dinero y de dónde sale.

cards.title: Para qué sirve el dinero
cards.text: El dinero tiene tres funciones: medio de intercambio (con él puedes comprar), unidad de cuenta (los precios se miden en él) y depósito de valor (conserva su valor con el tiempo).

deep.x: Economists define money by what it does, not what it's made of. Anything that does these three jobs well enough can serve as money: shells, cigarettes, gold or numbers in a bank database.

items: Medium of exchange: you can pay with it
Unit of account: prices are measured in it
Store of value: it keeps worth over time

deep.x: When a job fails

x: In hyperinflation, money fails as a store of value: people spend it instantly or switch to dollars
In prisoner-of-war camps, cigarettes became the unit of account and medium of exchange
Bitcoin works poorly as a unit of account because its price swings so much

deep.x: Why a unit of account matters
Without a common measure, every good would need a price in every other good. With 1,000 goods, that's nearly 500,000 exchange rates; with money, just 1,000 prices.

items: price of fish in bread, in shoes, in wine...
one price per good, in euros

deep.x: Money is a social agreement: it works because everyone expects everyone else to accept it.

cards.title: Del trueque a las apps
cards.text: El trueque exige una doble coincidencia de deseos: tienes que encontrar a alguien que tenga lo que tú quieres y que quiera lo que tú tienes. El dinero resolvió ese problema.

deep.x: Barter requires a "double coincidence of wants": the person with what you want must also want what you have. Money removed that problem and let trade expand enormously.
Steps in the story

x: Commodity money: shells, salt, cattle, metal by weight
Coins: standard weight and stamp, so no need to weigh
Paper notes: receipts for gold held by banks or goldsmiths
Bank money: cheques, transfers, cards
Digital: instant payments, mobile apps, contactless

deep.x: Did barter economies exist?
Anthropologists have found few societies that ran mainly on barter. Many communities used credit and obligations ("you owe me one") long before coins.
Portugal's escudo was replaced by the euro at a fixed rate of 200.482 escudos per euro; notes and coins arrived on 1 January 2002.

cards.title: Dinero fiduciario

items: el euro y el dólar de hoy

cards.text: Los billetes de euro no están respaldados por oro. Su valor procede de la confianza y de la ley: los gobiernos los aceptan para pagar impuestos y obligan a aceptarlos para saldar deudas.

deep.x: "Fiat" means "let it be done" in Latin. Fiat money has value because a government declares it legal tender and people trust it, not because it can be exchanged for gold.
Where value comes from

x: Legal tender: it must be accepted to settle debts
Taxes: the state demands payment in its currency
Trust in institutions and in stable prices

deep.x: The end of gold
In August 1971, US President Nixon ended the convertibility of dollars into gold, effectively ending the Bretton Woods system. Since then, all major currencies have been fiat.
The risk

items.b: independent central banks with inflation targets

deep.w: Money backed by gold is safer
deep.r: the gold standard caused rigid policy and worsened depressions such as the 1930s

cards.title: Casi todo el dinero es digital

viz.unit: % del dinero de la zona euro (aprox.)

cards.text: Los billetes y monedas físicos son una pequeña parte de la masa monetaria. La mayor parte del dinero existe como números en cuentas bancarias, creados cuando los bancos prestan.

deep.x: Cash is only a small part of the money in the economy. Most money exists as bank deposits: numbers in accounts, created mainly when banks make loans.
How banks create money

When a bank grants you a €100,000 mortgage, it doesn't hand over other customers' savings. It credits your account with a new deposit. New money has been created; it disappears when the loan is repaid.

steps: Money spent and moves between banks

deep.x: What limits it

x: Demand for loans from creditworthy borrowers
Capital and liquidity rules for banks
Interest rates set by the central bank

deep.x: Official confirmation
The Bank of England explained this in a widely cited 2014 article, "Money creation in the modern economy", correcting the textbook picture of banks just lending out savings.
Every time a bank lends, it creates money; every time a loan is repaid, money disappears.

cards.title: Bancos centrales

steps: Cambia el coste de los préstamos

cards.text: El Banco Central Europeo fija los tipos de interés de la zona euro con el objetivo de una inflación cercana al 2 % anual. El Banco de Portugal forma parte de este sistema.

deep.x: A central bank manages a currency: it sets key interest rates, supervises banks and acts as lender of last resort. For the euro, that's the European Central Bank (ECB) in Frankfurt.
The Eurosystem

items: National central banks: Banco de Portugal, Bundesbank, Banque de France and others
Governing Council: sets policy for the euro area

deep.x: The 2% target

Since its 2021 strategy review, the ECB aims for inflation of 2% over the medium term, treating deviations above and below as equally undesirable. A little inflation is preferred to zero because it gives room to cut rates and avoids deflation.
Recent history
Banco de Portugal's role

x: Represents Portugal in ECB decisions
Supervises Portuguese banks and payment systems
Issues euro notes in Portugal and publishes economic forecasts

deep.x: Many Portuguese mortgages have variable rates linked to Euribor, so ECB decisions show up in family budgets within months.

cards.title: Inflación
cards.text: La inflación significa que los precios suben con el tiempo, así que cada euro compra menos. Al 2 % anual, los precios se duplican en unos 35 años.

deep.x: Inflation is the general rise in prices over time. It's measured with a basket of typical goods and services; in Portugal, INE publishes the consumer price index (CPI) monthly.
Causes

items.b: too much spending chasing too few goods
workers and firms anticipate price rises

deep.x: The 2021–2023 surge
Reopening after COVID, supply chain disruptions and the energy shock after Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 pushed euro-area inflation above 10% in late 2022.
Hyperinflation

x: Germany, 1923: prices doubled every few days
Hungary, 1946: the worst recorded, prices doubled roughly every 15 hours
Zimbabwe, 2008: 100-trillion-dollar notes

deep.x: At 2% a year, prices double in about 35 years: steady, small inflation still adds up.

cards.title: La regla del 72
cards.text: Divide 72 entre un porcentaje anual para estimar cuántos años tarda algo en duplicarse. Sirve para precios, ahorros y deudas.

deep.x: The rule of 72 is a quick mental shortcut: divide 72 by a yearly percentage to estimate how many years it takes something to double.

items.m: works well for rates of about 2–15%

deep.x: Examples
Why 72?
The exact number is about 69.3 (from the natural log of 2), but 72 is close and divides easily by 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 12.
It works in reverse

x: To double in 10 years you need about 7.2% a year
Prices rising 6% a year halve your cash's buying power in about 12 years
72 / 9% = 8 years

deep.x: Variants exist: some use 70 for low rates and 69.3 for continuous compounding.

cards.title: Interés
cards.text: El interés es el precio del dinero. Quien pide prestado lo paga; quien ahorra lo cobra. Unos tipos más altos del banco central suelen significar préstamos más caros y mejor remuneración del ahorro.

deep.x: Interest is the price of using someone else's money for a while. Borrowers pay it; savers and lenders earn it.
What sets the rate

x: Central bank rates: the baseline
Risk: riskier borrowers pay more
Time: longer loans usually cost more
Inflation expectations: lenders want compensation

deep.x: Typical rates
When rates rise
TAN and TAEG
In Portugal, loan offers show TAN (nominal annual rate) and TAEG (annual percentage rate of charge, including fees and insurance). Compare loans by TAEG.
Compare the total cost (TAEG), not just the headline rate.

cards.title: Oferta y demanda
cards.text: Los precios suben cuando mucha gente quiere algo escaso y bajan cuando abunda o nadie lo quiere. Las entradas de conciertos y los vuelos de verano son ejemplos clásicos.

deep.x: Prices are set where the quantity people want to buy meets the quantity sellers want to sell. When either side shifts, prices move.
Examples

x: Summer flights and August hotels in the Algarve cost more: demand peaks
Strawberries are cheap in season: supply is plentiful
Concert tickets sell out and resale prices soar when demand far exceeds seats
Olive oil prices roughly doubled in 2023–24 after droughts cut Spanish harvests

deep.x: Elasticity
Price controls
Rent controls are a classic debate: they protect current tenants but can reduce the supply and upkeep of rental housing.

cards.title: La inflación se come el efectivo
cards.text: 10 000 € guardados bajo el colchón durante 10 años con un 3 % de inflación comprarían lo que hoy compran unos 7400 €.

deep.x: Money that sits idle loses buying power every year inflation is positive. Cash under the mattress is "safe" only in nominal terms.
Real value
Real value = amount / (1 + inflation)^years
Protecting savings

x: Interest-bearing savings accounts or deposits
Portuguese government savings products (Certificados de Aforro, Certificados do Tesouro)
Long-term investments for money you won't need for years

deep.x: But keep some cash
Keep an emergency fund in easy-access savings, and put longer-term money to work.
Idle cash has a hidden cost: inflation.

quiz.q: Con una inflación del 2 %, ¿cuánto tardan más o menos los precios en duplicarse?
¿Qué da valor hoy a los billetes de euro?

lessons.title: Presupuestos
lessons.summary: Tomar decisiones de dinero a propósito.

cards.title: Págate a ti primero
cards.text: Aparta el ahorro en cuanto llegue el sueldo, no con lo que sobre a final de mes: casi nunca sobra nada.

deep.x: "Pay yourself first" means moving money to savings as soon as your salary arrives, before spending on anything else. Saving what's left at month-end rarely works, because there's rarely anything left.
Automate it
Why it works

x: Removes the daily decision and willpower
You adapt spending to what's in the current account
Savings grow steadily, even in small amounts

deep.x: Start small
Even 5% of take-home pay builds the habit. Increase it by one or two percentage points each year or with each raise.

Behavioural economists Richard Thaler and Shlomo Benartzi's "Save More Tomorrow" scheme, which commits future raises to savings, lifted participants' savings rates from about 3.5% to over 13% in a few years.

cards.title: La regla 50/30/20
cards.text: Un reparto inicial sencillo del sueldo neto: 50 % para necesidades, 30 % para caprichos y 20 % para ahorrar o pagar deudas. Ajústalo a tu situación.

deep.x: The 50/30/20 rule, popularised by Elizabeth Warren and Amelia Warren Tyagi in their 2005 book "All Your Worth", is a simple starting split of take-home pay.
Applied to €1,500 a month

items.b: €300: emergency fund, investing, extra debt payments

deep.x: Adjusting it

x: High rents in Lisbon or Porto may push needs well above 50%
Paying off expensive debt can justify more than 20% to the last bucket
Higher incomes can save much more than 20%

deep.x: It's a guide
A rough budget you follow beats a perfect one you abandon.

cards.title: Necesidades y caprichos

items.b: necesidad, pero el último modelo es capricho

cards.text: Las necesidades son lo que tienes que pagar sí o sí (alquiler, comida, transporte, facturas). Los caprichos hacen la vida más agradable, pero son opcionales. Muchas cosas tienen una parte de necesidad y otra de capricho.

deep.x: Needs are expenses you must pay to live and work. Wants make life nicer but are optional. Many purchases mix both.

items.b: need, but a bigger flat is a want
need, but a new car is often a want
need, but takeaway is a want
need, but the latest model is a want

deep.x: Spotting the want part
Ask: what's the cheapest way to meet this need? The difference between that and what you spend is the want.

x: Monthly phone plan €35
Cheapest adequate plan €12
Want part: €23 a month = €276 a year

deep.x: Not about deprivation

x: Wants are good: they make life enjoyable
The goal is choosing wants consciously
Cut wants you don't value to fund ones you do

deep.x: Spend freely on what you love; cut ruthlessly on what you don't.

cards.title: Fondo de emergencia
cards.text: Ten entre tres y seis meses de gastos esenciales en una cuenta de ahorro de acceso fácil. Convierte una crisis, como perder el trabajo o una avería del coche, en un simple contratiempo.

deep.x: An emergency fund is money set aside for unexpected costs or loss of income. It's the foundation of financial stability.

items.l: EU deposit guarantee per person per bank

deep.x: What it's for
How much

x: Stable job, no dependants: around three months
Self-employed, single income, or children: six months or more
Count essential expenses, not total spending

deep.x: Building it
Where to keep it
Keep it in an easy-access savings account at a bank covered by the deposit guarantee. Investments can fall just when you need the money.
Without an emergency fund, a broken car often ends up on a credit card at high interest, turning a one-off cost into months of debt.

cards.title: Primero, apunta
cards.text: Casi todo el mundo subestima los gastos pequeños y frecuentes. Apunta cada gasto durante un mes antes de hacer un presupuesto; el resultado suele sorprender.

deep.x: Before making a budget, track every expense for a month. Most people underestimate small, frequent spending, and the results are often surprising.
How to track

x: Banking apps that categorise spending automatically
A simple spreadsheet
A notebook for cash
Review bank and card statements

deep.x: What usually surprises people
After tracking
You can't manage what you don't measure.

cards.title: Las suscripciones se acumulan
cards.text: Streaming, apps, gimnasio y almacenamiento en la nube: 8 € por aquí, 12 € por allá, y quizá pagues cosas que no usas. Revisa los extractos del banco y cancela lo que hayas olvidado.

deep.x: Subscriptions are designed to be easy to start and easy to forget. Small monthly charges add up to large yearly sums.
Why they creep

x: Free trials that roll into paid plans
Annual renewals you forget about
Price increases without notice you notice
Sharing services you no longer use

deep.x: An audit
Rotating
Instead of paying for several streaming services at once, subscribe to one, watch what you want, cancel, then switch.
EU consumer rules are pushing for easier online cancellation, so cancelling should be as easy as signing up.

cards.title: El «efecto café», en perspectiva
cards.text: Los pequeños ahorros diarios suman, pero las grandes decisiones, como el alquiler, el coche y la vivienda, pesan más. Optimiza esas tres antes de agobiarte por un café.

deep.x: The "latte factor", popularised by author David Bach, says small daily savings grow into large sums. True, but big decisions matter much more.
The big three
These typically make up most spending. A 10% saving on rent beats giving up every coffee.
Small savings still help

x: They build awareness and habits
Invested over decades, small amounts grow
But they shouldn't cause misery

deep.x: Balance
Get the big decisions right, then enjoy your coffee.

cards.title: Contabilidad mental

items.w: «Es un extra, puedo fundírmelo»
items.r: «Un euro es un euro: ¿encaja en mi plan?»

cards.text: Tratamos el dinero de forma distinta según de dónde venga: la devolución de Hacienda parece «dinero gratis» y se gasta. Un euro es un euro, venga de donde venga.

deep.x: Mental accounting, a concept developed by economist Richard Thaler, describes how people treat money differently depending on its source or label, even though money is interchangeable.

items.w: "My tax refund is free money to spend"
items.r: "A euro is a euro: it could pay debt or build savings"

deep.x: Common examples

x: Spending a bonus freely while carrying credit card debt
Keeping savings at 1% while paying 18% on a card
Splurging with casino winnings ("house money")
Treating refunds as gifts rather than your own money

deep.x: Using it to your advantage

items.b: commit in advance to save half

deep.x: Nobel recognition
Thaler received the 2017 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for his work in behavioural economics, including mental accounting.
Treat every euro the same, whatever its source.

cards.title: Inflación del estilo de vida
cards.text: Cuando sube el sueldo, el gasto tiende a subir al mismo ritmo. Ahorrar la mitad de cada aumento permite que tu nivel de vida mejore mientras tus ahorros crecen más deprisa.

deep.x: When income rises, spending often rises to match it. People with higher pay can end up no better off, just with more expensive habits.
Why it happens

x: New expenses quickly feel normal
Social comparison with peers
Fixed commitments (rent, car loans) are hard to reverse

deep.x: The half rule
Your lifestyle still improves, while savings grow faster.
Over a career
Let your lifestyle grow more slowly than your income.

cards.title: Un presupuesto sencillo
cards.text: Sueldo neto: 1600 €. Necesidades 800 €, caprichos 480 €, ahorro 320 €. A los seis meses, 1920 € ahorrados: un primer paso hacia el fondo de emergencia.

deep.x: A worked example with €1,600 take-home pay, using the 50/30/20 split.
Breaking down needs
Six-month result

x: €320 saved per month
× 6 months

deep.x: That's already more than one month of essential expenses: a solid start on an emergency fund.
Adjusting

x: If rent is higher, trim wants first
Review the budget monthly for the first few months
Increase savings when income rises

deep.x: A budget isn't a restriction; it's a plan for your money.

quiz.q: ¿De qué tamaño suele recomendarse un fondo de emergencia?
En la regla 50/30/20, ¿para qué es el 20 %?

cards.title: Simple y compuesto
cards.text: El interés simple solo se paga sobre lo que aportas. El compuesto también se paga sobre los intereses anteriores, así que el crecimiento se acelera con el tiempo.

deep.x: Simple interest pays only on your original amount. Compound interest pays on the original plus all interest already earned, so growth accelerates over time.
Side by side
Year by year
With simple interest, the yearly interest stays €50 forever.
Compounding frequency
Interest can compound yearly, monthly or daily. More frequent compounding gives slightly more; the effective annual rate (TAE in Portugal) shows the true yearly result.
Compounding is slow at first and powerful later: time is its fuel.

cards.title: La fórmula
cards.text: Al cabo de n años, el dinero se multiplica por el factor (1 + r) cada año. Pequeñas diferencias en r o en n producen diferencias enormes.

deep.x: Compound growth multiplies your money by the same factor each year. The formula shows why rate and time matter so much.
Sensitivity
A two-point difference in yearly return nearly doubles the final amount over 30 years.
Working backwards
PV = FV / (1 + r)^n

x: Want €50,000 in 20 years at 5%
≈ €18,840 needed today

deep.x: Spreadsheet tip

x: Excel and Google Sheets: =FV(rate, years, payment, -present value)
Or simply: =amount*(1+rate)^years

deep.x: The exponent is where the magic lives: n matters more than you expect.

cards.title: 1000 € al 5 %
cards.text: A los 10 años: 1629 €. A los 20: 2653 €. A los 40: 7040 €. La mayor parte del crecimiento llega al final.

deep.x: Watching €1,000 grow at 5% a year shows how compounding accelerates. Most of the growth arrives in the later years.
The hockey stick
The last decade adds more than four times as much as the first.
Doubling
By the rule of 72, money at 5% doubles roughly every 14 years: €1,000, €2,000, €4,000, €8,000.
Why patience pays

x: Early years feel slow and discouraging
Many people stop before the curve steepens
Staying invested lets the later years do the heavy lifting

deep.x: In compounding, the best years are always at the end.

cards.title: El tiempo gana a la cantidad
cards.text: Empezar pronto importa más que invertir mucho. Quien invierte de los 25 a los 35 y luego para puede acabar con más que quien invierte de los 35 a los 65, con la misma rentabilidad.

deep.x: Starting early can beat investing more later, because early money has more years to compound.

v.unit: pot at 65, € thousands (€2,000 a year at 7%)

deep.x: The two savers

items.b: invests €2,000 a year from 25 to 35, then stops, €20,000 total
invests €2,000 a year from 35 to 65, €60,000 total

deep.x: Ana ends up with more, despite investing a third as much, because her money compounds for 40 years.
The assumption
This example uses 7% a year, roughly the long-run nominal return of a diversified share portfolio. At lower returns the effect is smaller, but starting early still helps a lot.
The lesson
The most powerful variable in compounding is the one you can't get back: time.

cards.title: Deuda que se compone
cards.text: En las deudas, el interés compuesto juega en tu contra. El saldo de una tarjeta de crédito puede costar un 15–20 % anual o más, y duplicarse en unos cuatro o cinco años si no se paga.

deep.x: Compounding works against you when you owe money. High-interest debt grows quickly if unpaid.
Doubling time
By the rule of 72, debt at 18% doubles in about four years. Credit card and some consumer loan rates in Portugal can exceed 15–20% TAEG.
Why it's dangerous

x: Minimum payments may barely cover interest
Late fees add to the balance
The longer it runs, the faster it grows

deep.x: Turning it around

steps: Then invest at lower, uncertain returns

deep.x: Paying off 18% debt is the best guaranteed "investment" available.

cards.title: Las comisiones importan
cards.text: Una comisión anual del 1 % parece minúscula, pero también se compone. En 30 años puede llevarse alrededor de una cuarta parte de tu capital final.

deep.x: Fees compound too, quietly reducing your returns every year. A small-sounding yearly fee can take a large share of your final pot.
The share lost
Where fees hide
Low-cost options
Index funds and ETFs typically charge 0.1–0.3% a year, compared with 1–2% for many actively managed funds sold through banks.
Before investing, ask for the KID (Key Information Document), which EU rules require for many investment products and which shows costs.

cards.title: Nominal y real
cards.text: Una rentabilidad del 5 % con un 3 % de inflación supone solo un 2 % aproximado de crecimiento real del poder adquisitivo. Compara siempre la rentabilidad con la inflación.

deep.x: Nominal returns are the numbers you see. Real returns subtract inflation, showing how much your buying power actually grew.
Precise version
Real = (1 + nominal) / (1 + inflation) − 1

x: ≈ 2% real

deep.x: Examples
The middle case is Portugal in 2022, when inflation reached 7.8%.
Why it matters

x: Long-term goals are about what money can buy, not the number of euros
Cash that looks safe can lose real value
Compare investment returns with inflation, not zero

deep.x: Always ask: after inflation, did I actually get richer?

cards.title: ¿La frase de Einstein?

items.w: Einstein lo llamó la octava maravilla
items.r: No hay pruebas de que lo dijera

cards.text: «El interés compuesto es la octava maravilla del mundo» se atribuye a menudo a Einstein, pero no hay pruebas de que lo dijera. Las matemáticas son reales de todos modos.

deep.x: "Compound interest is the eighth wonder of the world. He who understands it, earns it; he who doesn't, pays it." It's often credited to Albert Einstein, but there's no evidence he said it.

items.w: "Einstein called compound interest the eighth wonder of the world"
items.r: No reliable source links the quote to Einstein

deep.x: How the myth spread

Researchers who track quotations, such as the Quote Investigator website, have found no record of the line in Einstein's writings or contemporary reports. Similar claims appeared in finance articles decades after his death.
Why it sticks
Misattribution is common

x: Einstein is credited with many quotes he never said
Others include "insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results"

deep.x: The maths is real
Whoever said it, the principle stands: compounding rewards savers and punishes borrowers.
Check famous quotes before repeating them; the maths needs no celebrity.

cards.title: Aportaciones periódicas
cards.text: Aportar una cantidad fija cada mes, en lugar de todo de golpe, suaviza los altibajos del mercado. Se llama promediar el coste en euros.

deep.x: Investing a fixed amount every month, rather than trying to time the market, smooths out price swings. It's called euro-cost (or dollar-cost) averaging.
Example
The average cost per share (€15) is lower than the average price (€16.67).
Lump sum vs regular

items: historically wins about two-thirds of the time, since markets usually rise

deep.x: A 2012 Vanguard study found investing a lump sum immediately beat spreading it out about two-thirds of the time. But for most people investing from salary, monthly investing is simply natural.
Benefits

x: Builds a habit
Removes the urge to time the market
Works automatically

deep.x: Regular investing turns market falls into buying opportunities.

cards.title: 100 € al mes
cards.text: Invertir 100 € al mes al 5 % anual durante 30 años: aportas 36 000 € y se convierten en unos 83 000 €.

deep.x: Small, regular amounts grow into significant sums over decades, thanks to compounding.

v.unit: €100 a month at 5% a year, € thousands

deep.x: Paid in vs grown
Increasing over time
If you raise the monthly amount by just 3% a year, in line with pay rises, the 30-year result grows to around €118,000.
Making it happen
Start with what you can; consistency matters more than size.

quiz.q: ¿Qué diferencia el interés compuesto del simple?
Según la regla del 72, ¿cuánto tarda el dinero en duplicarse al 6 %?

cards.title: Ahorrar e invertir
cards.text: Ahorrar mantiene el dinero seguro a corto plazo. Invertir es comprar activos que pueden crecer a largo plazo, con el riesgo de que pierdan valor por el camino.

deep.x: Saving keeps money safe and available. Investing puts money into assets that can grow over time but may fall in value along the way. Both have a place.
Which for what
Safe savings options in Portugal
The cost of only saving
Over long periods, savings at low interest may barely beat inflation. Investing gives money a chance to grow in real terms.
Save for the next few years; invest for the next few decades.

cards.title: Acciones

items.b: lo que pagan hoy los compradores

cards.text: Una acción es una pequeña parte de la propiedad de una empresa. Puedes ganar si su precio sube y si reparte dividendos, y perder si baja.

deep.x: A share is a small slice of ownership in a company. Shareholders benefit if the company's value rises and if it pays dividends.

items.b: sell for more than you paid
price can fall, company can fail

deep.x: Where returns come from
Risks

x: A single company can lose most of its value or go bankrupt
Prices swing with news and sentiment
Diversification reduces single-company risk

deep.x: Portuguese examples
Listed Portuguese companies include EDP, Galp, Jerónimo Martins and BCP. Most investors also hold international shares for diversification.
Dividends reinvested over decades account for a large share of total stock market returns.

cards.title: Bonos

steps: Te devuelven el dinero al vencimiento

cards.text: Un bono es un préstamo a un gobierno o a una empresa. Te pagan intereses y te devuelven el dinero al final. Suelen ser más estables que las acciones, con menor rentabilidad a largo plazo.

deep.x: A bond is a loan to a government or company. In return, the borrower pays regular interest (the coupon) and repays the amount at maturity.
Types
Prices and rates
In 2022, as rates jumped, many bond funds had their worst year in decades.
Credit risk

items.b: higher than Germany, much improved since 2012

deep.x: Portugal's crisis
In early 2012, Portuguese 10-year government bond yields rose above 15% as investors feared default. By the 2020s they were close to Spain's and well below Italy's at times.
Bonds are steadier than shares, not risk-free.

cards.title: Riesgo y rentabilidad
cards.text: Una mayor rentabilidad esperada viene con mayores vaivenes. No hay una forma fiable de conseguir rentabilidades altas sin aceptar riesgo.

deep.x: Higher expected returns come with bigger swings in value. There's no reliable way to get high returns without taking more risk.
Measuring risk
Your risk tolerance
Mixing assets
A mix of shares and bonds offers a middle path: lower swings than all shares, higher expected return than all bonds.

deep.r: cash has low volatility but high inflation risk over the long term

cards.title: Diversificación
cards.text: No pongas todos los huevos en la misma cesta. Repartir el dinero entre muchas empresas, países y tipos de activos reduce el daño que puede hacer cualquier fallo aislado.

deep.x: Diversification spreads your money across many investments so that a single failure doesn't sink you. It's often called the only free lunch in investing.
Why it works
Different investments don't all fall at the same time or by the same amount. Combining them smooths overall returns.
Home bias

items: most money in your own country
Portugal is a tiny fraction of 1% of world markets

deep.x: Many investors overweight their own country. Portugal is a tiny share of global markets, so a Portugal-only portfolio is concentrated.
Limits

x: In crashes, many assets fall together
Diversification reduces risk but doesn't eliminate it
Too many overlapping funds add cost without adding diversification

deep.x: Don't put all your eggs in one basket, or one country.

cards.title: Fondos indexados

items: suele quedar por debajo del índice

cards.text: Un fondo indexado compra todas las empresas de un índice, como el S&P 500 o un índice mundial, con un coste muy bajo. La mayoría de los fondos de gestión activa no consiguen batir a su índice a largo plazo.

deep.x: An index fund buys all the companies in an index, such as the S&P 500 or a world index, instead of trying to pick winners. It's cheap, simple and hard to beat.
The evidence
S&P Dow Jones Indices' SPIVA reports consistently find that around 90% of actively managed US large-company funds underperform the S&P 500 over 15-year periods. European results are similar.
Origins
John Bogle founded Vanguard and launched the first index fund for ordinary investors in 1976. It was mocked as "Bogle's folly" at the time.
Why index funds win
Choosing one

x: Global index for broad diversification
Low TER
Large fund size
Accumulating or distributing to suit you

deep.x: Warren Buffett has repeatedly recommended low-cost index funds for most investors.

cards.title: Tiempo en el mercado

items.w: «Esperaré al momento perfecto»
items.r: Estar en el mercado gana a adivinar el momento

cards.text: Los mercados caen a menudo, a veces con fuerza, pero históricamente se han recuperado y han crecido a largo plazo. Perderse solo los mejores días puede dañar mucho la rentabilidad.

deep.x: "Time in the market beats timing the market." Markets fall often, sometimes sharply, but have historically recovered and grown over long periods. Missing just a few of the best days can badly hurt returns.

items.w: "I'll sell before the crash and buy back before the recovery"
items.r: Nobody reliably times both, staying invested has historically won

deep.x: The best days

Analyses of the S&P 500 by J.P. Morgan Asset Management show that missing just the 10 best days over a 20-year period roughly halved the annual return. Many of the best days came shortly after the worst.
Why timing fails

x: You need to be right twice: when to sell and when to buy
Best and worst days cluster together
Emotions push you to sell low and buy high

deep.x: Staying invested is boring, and boring tends to work.

cards.title: Demasiado bueno para ser verdad
cards.text: Las promesas de rentabilidades altas garantizadas son una señal de alarma. Si está garantizada, es baja; si es alta, no está garantizada. Las estafas suelen meter prisa y pedir secreto.

deep.x: High guaranteed returns don't exist. "If it's guaranteed, it's low; if it's high, it isn't guaranteed."
Classic schemes

items.b: early investors paid with new investors' money
hype a cheap share then sell

deep.x: Famous cases

x: Bernie Madoff's Ponzi scheme, uncovered in 2008, involved about $65 billion in fictitious account balances
In 1980s Portugal, "Dona Branca" promised depositors 10% a month before her scheme collapsed

deep.x: Checks
If someone promises high returns with no risk, the risk is that they're lying.

cards.title: Emociones e inversión
cards.text: El miedo hace vender tras los desplomes y la codicia hace comprar en los máximos: justo lo contrario de «comprar barato, vender caro». Un plan por escrito te ayuda a mantener el rumbo.

deep.x: Fear and greed push investors to buy high and sell low, the opposite of what they intend.
The behaviour gap
Studies such as Morningstar's "Mind the Gap" find investors earn less than the funds they own, by around one percentage point a year, because of poorly timed buying and selling.
Defences
Rebalancing
Rebalancing forces you to sell high and buy low, mechanically.
Your biggest investment risk may be your own reactions.

cards.title: Antes de invertir
cards.text: Un orden habitual: liquidar la deuda cara, crear un fondo de emergencia y después invertir el dinero que no vayas a necesitar en al menos cinco años. Esto es información general, no asesoramiento personal.

deep.x: A common order of priorities helps make sure investing doesn't put your stability at risk. This is general information, not personal advice.

steps: Invest money not needed for 5+ years

deep.x: Checklist
Why five years
Shares can fall sharply and take years to recover. Money needed sooner shouldn't depend on markets.
Getting started
Banks sometimes sell complex or costly products; independent comparison and asking about all fees helps.

quiz.q: ¿Qué es una acción?
options: Una pequeña parte de la propiedad

quiz.q: ¿Por qué diversificar?
options: Para reducir el daño de cualquier fallo aislado
quiz.explain: No pongas todos los huevos en la misma cesta.

lessons.title: Economía cotidiana
lessons.summary: Las grandes ideas detrás de las noticias.

cards.title: PIB
cards.text: El producto interior bruto es el valor total de los bienes y servicios que un país produce en un año. Mide el tamaño de una economía, no su bienestar.

deep.x: Gross domestic product (GDP) is the total value of goods and services produced in a country in a year. It measures the size of an economy and how fast it's growing.
Portugal's economy

items.l: GDP per person vs EU average, adjusted for prices

deep.x: What GDP misses
Its inventor's warning
Economist Simon Kuznets, who developed national income accounts in the 1930s, warned that "the welfare of a nation can scarcely be inferred from a measurement of national income".
Per person
GDP per person, adjusted for price levels (PPP), is a better guide to living standards than total GDP.
GDP measures output, not happiness, but output pays for much of what we value.

cards.title: Recesión
cards.text: Una recesión es una caída importante de la actividad económica, que a menudo se define como dos trimestres seguidos de caída del PIB. El empleo y los ingresos suelen resentirse.

deep.x: A recession is a significant, widespread fall in economic activity. A common rule of thumb is two consecutive quarters of falling GDP.
Portugal's recent recessions
Official definitions
In the US, a committee of the National Bureau of Economic Research decides recession dates using many indicators, not just GDP. In Europe, the two-quarter rule is widely used.
What helps
Depression
A depression is a very deep, long recession, like the 1930s Great Depression.
Recessions are a normal, if painful, part of the economic cycle.

cards.title: Coste de oportunidad
cards.text: El coste real de algo es aquello a lo que renuncias para conseguirlo. Una tarde de estudio cuesta la salida que no hiciste.

deep.x: The real cost of any choice is the best alternative you give up. Money, time and attention can only be spent once.

items.b: what the money could have earned invested

deep.x: Money example

x: €20,000 car instead of investing
At 5% for 10 years, that's about €32,600
Opportunity cost ≈ €12,600 of growth

deep.x: Not just money

x: Time spent scrolling is time not spent sleeping or exercising
A business's resources used for one project can't fund another

deep.x: Better decisions
Thinking about opportunity cost helps compare options fairly, rather than judging each in isolation.
Every yes is a no to something else.

cards.title: Incentivos
cards.text: La gente responde a los incentivos. Los impuestos a las bebidas azucaradas reducen las ventas; los depósitos por envase aumentan el reciclaje. Los mal diseñados salen el tiro por la culata.

deep.x: People respond to incentives: rewards and penalties change behaviour. Well-designed incentives help; badly designed ones backfire.
Examples that worked
Backfiring incentives

x: The "cobra effect": a bounty on cobras reportedly led people to breed them
Paying by lines of code encourages bloated software
Targets for hospital waiting times can encourage gaming the numbers

deep.x: Designing incentives
Tell me how someone is paid, and I'll tell you how they behave.

cards.title: Ventaja comparativa
cards.text: Los países ganan especializándose en lo que hacen relativamente mejor y comerciando, aunque uno sea mejor en todo. El vino y los paños de Portugal e Inglaterra fueron el ejemplo de Ricardo en 1817.

deep.x: Countries gain from trade by specialising in what they're relatively best at, even if one country is better at everything. This is comparative advantage.
Ricardo's insight

In David Ricardo's 1817 example, Portugal is better at producing both wine and cloth. But it's relatively better at wine, while England's disadvantage is smaller in cloth. If Portugal makes wine and England cloth, and they trade, both have more.
Absolute vs comparative

items.b: produce more with the same resources

deep.x: Real history

x: The 1703 Methuen Treaty between England and Portugal lowered duties on Portuguese wine and English cloth
Port wine became an English favourite
Some historians argue it held back Portuguese manufacturing

deep.x: Specialise in what you give up least to do, and trade for the rest.

cards.title: La tragedia de los comunes

steps: Cada uno coge un poco más

cards.text: Cuando un recurso compartido es gratis para todos, todo el mundo lo sobreexplota. La sobrepesca es un ejemplo clásico; las cuotas y las normas de propiedad pueden ayudar.

deep.x: When a shared resource is open to all, each user has an incentive to take more, even though overuse harms everyone. Ecologist Garrett Hardin popularised the idea in 1968.
Classic example
In 1992, Canada closed the Grand Banks cod fishery after stocks collapsed, costing around 30,000 jobs. The cod have still not fully recovered.
Solutions
Ostrom's discovery
Economist Elinor Ostrom, who won the 2009 Nobel Prize in Economics, showed that many communities successfully manage commons for centuries through local rules, monitoring and sanctions.
Portugal
Portuguese sardine catches have been strictly limited in recent years under quotas agreed with Spain after stocks fell to historic lows, and stocks have since recovered.
Shared resources need shared rules.

cards.title: Impuestos
cards.text: Los impuestos financian los servicios públicos. Portugal aplica un impuesto sobre la renta (IRS) con tipos que suben con los ingresos, el IVA sobre las compras, con un tipo general del 23 % en el continente, y cotizaciones a la seguridad social.

deep.x: Taxes fund public services. Portugal raises money mainly through income tax, social security contributions and IVA.
Regional IVA
Where the money comes from
Fairness debates

x: Progressive income tax asks more from higher earners
IVA falls more heavily on lower earners, who spend more of their income
Tax evasion shifts the burden onto honest taxpayers

deep.x: Taxes are how a society pays for what it decides to do together.

cards.title: Desempleo
cards.text: Cierto desempleo es normal porque la gente cambia de trabajo. La tasa es la proporción de personas que quieren trabajar y buscan empleo, pero no lo tienen.

deep.x: The unemployment rate is the share of people who want work and are actively looking for it but don't have a job. Some unemployment is normal as people move between jobs.
Portugal's rate
Types
Who isn't counted

x: Students and retirees
People who've given up looking ("discouraged workers")
Those working fewer hours than they'd like are counted as employed

deep.x: Youth unemployment in Portugal is typically two to three times the overall rate.

cards.title: Tipos de cambio
cards.text: El tipo de cambio es el precio de una moneda en otra. Un euro más fuerte abarata las vacaciones en el extranjero, pero encarece las exportaciones portuguesas para los extranjeros.

deep.x: An exchange rate is the price of one currency in another. It affects holidays, imports, exports and investments.
Euro–dollar history
What moves rates
Effects on Portugal

x: Oil and many commodities are priced in dollars, so a weak euro raises fuel costs
Tourism from the US and UK rises when the euro is weak
Exports outside the euro area become more competitive

deep.x: A currency's value is relative: strong for some, weak for others.

cards.title: Leer un titular

items.w: La inflación bajó, así que los precios son menores
items.r: Los precios siguieron subiendo, solo que más despacio

cards.text: «La inflación baja al 2 %» no significa que los precios hayan bajado, sino que suben más despacio. Solo una inflación negativa, llamada deflación, significa que los precios bajan.

deep.x: Economic headlines are easy to misread. "Inflation falls" doesn't mean prices fall; it means they rise more slowly.

items.w: "Inflation fell to 2%, so prices are dropping"
items.r: Prices are still rising, just by 2% a year instead of more

deep.x: Key distinctions
Deflation
Portugal briefly had deflation in 2009, when consumer prices fell about 0.8%. Japan experienced long periods of mild deflation from the 1990s.
Other tricky headlines

x: "GDP grows 0.5%": usually quarter-on-quarter, not yearly
"Unemployment rises" may reflect more people looking for work
Record highs in nominal terms may not be records after inflation

deep.x: Ask: is this a level or a rate, and compared to when?

quiz.q: ¿Qué es el coste de oportunidad?
options: Aquello a lo que renuncias para conseguir algo

quiz.q: Si la inflación baja del 5 % al 2 %, los precios…
quiz.explain: La deflación significaría precios a la baja.

cards.title: Deuda buena y deuda mala
cards.text: La deuda puede ser útil cuando compra algo que dura o gana valor, como una vivienda o la formación. La deuda cara para cosas que pierden valor rápido es más arriesgada.

deep.x: Debt isn't automatically bad. It lets you use future income today. Whether that helps depends on what you buy, what it costs and whether you can comfortably repay it.
Questions to ask

x: Will what I'm buying last longer than the loan?
Will it increase my income or reduce costs?
Can I afford the payments if my income drops?
What's the total cost including interest?

deep.x: Leverage cuts both ways

steps: Asset falls: losses magnified, debt remains

deep.x: "Good" debt can go bad

x: Too large a mortgage leaves no room for rate rises
Student loans for courses with weak job prospects
Business loans for an untested idea

deep.x: The question isn't "is debt good?" but "is this debt worth its cost and risk for me?"

cards.title: El coste real: la TAE
cards.text: Compara los préstamos por la TAE (TAEG en Portugal), que incluye los intereses y la mayoría de las comisiones como tasa anual. La cuota mensual más baja no siempre es el préstamo más barato.

deep.x: The headline interest rate rarely tells the full story. The APR, called TAEG in Portugal, combines interest and most fees into one yearly rate, so offers can be compared fairly.

items.b: annual rate including fees, insurance and charges
total amount payable by the consumer

deep.x: Example
Loan B looks dearer by its rate but is actually cheaper overall.
What's included

x: Interest
Opening and processing fees
Mandatory insurance linked to the loan
Account maintenance fees required by the loan

deep.x: Your rights

EU consumer credit rules require lenders to give you a standard information sheet (in Portugal, the FIN or Ficha de Informação Normalizada) before you sign, and give a 14-day right to withdraw from consumer credit agreements.
Always compare TAEG and the total amount payable, not the monthly payment.

cards.title: Más largo no es más barato
cards.text: Alargar un préstamo más años baja la cuota mensual, pero sube el total pagado. Un préstamo de 10 000 € al 8 % cuesta unos 2170 € de intereses a 5 años, pero 4560 € a 10.

deep.x: A longer loan term lowers each payment but means paying interest for more years. The total cost rises substantially.
Monthly payment vs total
The trap
Sellers often focus on the monthly payment: "only €121 a month!" Stretching the term makes expensive purchases feel affordable while costing far more.
For cars
A car loan longer than the car's useful life means you may still be paying for a car that needs replacing.
Choose the shortest term whose payment you can comfortably afford.

cards.title: La trampa del pago mínimo
cards.text: Pagar solo el mínimo de una tarjeta de crédito puede llevar muchos años y costar mucho más que la compra original. Los intereses siguen componiéndose sobre el saldo.

deep.x: Credit card minimum payments are designed to keep you paying interest for a long time. Paying only the minimum can take years and cost far more than the original purchase.
Why it's so slow
At 18% APR, a €3,000 balance generates about €45 of interest each month. If the minimum is little more than that, the debt barely moves.
Breaking the trap

x: Pay as much above the minimum as you can
Set up an automatic fixed payment, not the minimum
Stop adding new charges to the card
Consider a cheaper personal loan to clear it

deep.x: Revolving credit
In Portugal, many cards use "crédito revolving": the unpaid balance rolls over and accrues interest. Paying the full statement balance each month avoids interest entirely.

deep.w: Paying the minimum keeps you in good standing so it's fine
deep.r: it keeps you in debt for years at very high cost

cards.title: Bola de nieve o avalancha
cards.text: Dos formas de liquidar varias deudas: la bola de nieve paga primero el saldo más pequeño para lograr victorias rápidas; la avalancha paga primero el tipo más alto y ahorra más dinero.

deep.x: When you have several debts, the order you pay them off matters. Two popular methods take different approaches.
Example debts

x: Snowball: clear the €400 store card first, then the credit card, then the car
Avalanche: also starts with the store card here (highest rate), then the credit card

deep.x: The psychology
Research by Kellogg School of Management researchers found that people who focus on clearing individual accounts are more likely to pay off all their debt, because small wins build motivation.
Either way

steps: Roll that payment to the next

deep.x: The best method is the one you'll stick with; the avalanche saves the most money.

cards.title: Historial crediticio

items: No pidas muchos préstamos a la vez

cards.text: Los prestamistas revisan tu historial de préstamos y pagos. En Portugal, la central de riesgos del Banco de Portugal muestra tus responsabilidades con los bancos.

deep.x: Lenders want to know how you've handled credit before. In Portugal, the Banco de Portugal's Central Credit Register (CRC) records your loans and any missed payments.
How it works
Banks report credit responsibilities above €50 to the register each month. Lenders can check it before deciding on a loan.
Your rights

x: You can request your own report from Banco de Portugal free of charge, online
Errors can be corrected via the bank that reported them
Negative records remain for years, so missed payments have lasting effects

deep.x: Good habits
Unlike the US, Portugal doesn't use a single consumer "credit score" number publicly; lenders combine the register with their own assessments.

cards.title: Ratio de endeudamiento

viz.f: DSTI = pagos de deuda ÷ ingresos netos

cards.text: Los prestamistas miran qué parte de tus ingresos se va en pagar deudas. El Banco de Portugal recomienda que los bancos, en general, la mantengan en el 50 % o menos para los nuevos préstamos.

deep.x: The debt service-to-income ratio (DSTI) compares monthly debt payments with net monthly income. It's one of lenders' main checks on whether you can afford a new loan.
Banco de Portugal's guidance

Since 2018, Banco de Portugal's macroprudential measure recommends that banks generally limit new loans to borrowers whose DSTI is at or below 50%, with limited exceptions. It also caps loan-to-value at 90% for a primary home and limits loan terms.
Example

x: Net income €2,000
Mortgage €700 + car €200 = €900
DSTI = 45%

deep.x: Leave room
Lenders also test whether you could still pay if rates rose. You should too: a ratio near the limit leaves little margin for rate rises or emergencies.
Lenders' maximum isn't your comfortable level; aim lower.

cards.title: Compra ahora, paga después
cards.text: Dividir los pagos en plazos parece indoloro, pero facilita gastar y puede llevar a acumular obligaciones y recargos por demora.

deep.x: Buy now, pay later (BNPL) services split purchases into instalments, often interest-free if paid on time. They feel painless, and that's the risk.
Why it encourages spending

x: The full price feels smaller when split
Easy approval with little checking
Several plans across different shops are hard to track

deep.x: Risks

items: Debt not visible to other lenders

deep.x: Regulation
The EU's revised Consumer Credit Directive (2023) brings most BNPL services under consumer credit rules, including creditworthiness checks, with rules applying from late 2026.
If you couldn't afford it outright, splitting it doesn't make it affordable.

cards.title: El riesgo de avalar

items.w: «Es solo una firma»
items.r: Puede que tengas que pagar toda la deuda

cards.text: Ser avalista (fiador) significa que respondes si el prestatario no puede pagar. Avala solo lo que tú mismo podrías permitirte pagar.

deep.x: A guarantor (fiador in Portugal) promises to pay if the borrower doesn't. It's often asked of parents or friends for rentals or loans, and it's a serious commitment.

items.w: "It's just a formality to help a friend"
items.r: You're legally liable for the full debt if they can't pay

deep.x: What can happen

x: The lender can come to you for the full amount
It can appear on your credit register
It may limit your own ability to borrow
It can strain relationships

deep.x: Before signing
Renunciation of "benefício da excussão prévia"
Many Portuguese guarantee contracts require the guarantor to waive the right to insist the lender first pursue the borrower's assets. That means the lender can pursue you directly.

deep.w: Being a guarantor only matters if the borrower disappears
deep.r: illness, job loss or divorce can trigger it just as easily

deep.x: Only guarantee an amount you could afford to pay yourself.

cards.title: Liquidar una tarjeta
cards.text: 3000 € en una tarjeta al 18 % TAE. Pagando 100 € al mes tardas unos 40 meses y pagas ~1000 € de intereses. Pagando 200 €, bajas a unos 17 meses y ~420 €.

deep.x: A worked example: €3,000 on a credit card at 18% APR. How much you pay each month makes a huge difference.
Time to clear
Why doubling the payment more than halves the cost
Interest is charged on the remaining balance. Paying faster shrinks the balance faster, so each following month's interest is smaller.
A plan

x: Consider a lower-rate personal loan or balance transfer if available
Keep the card for emergencies only, or close it

deep.x: Every extra euro paid on high-interest debt is a guaranteed return at that rate.

quiz.q: ¿Qué incluye la TAE (TAEG)?
options: Intereses y la mayoría de comisiones, como tasa anual
quiz.explain: La forma justa de comparar préstamos.

quiz.q: ¿Qué método de pago de deudas ahorra más intereses?
Alargar un préstamo de 5 a 10 años normalmente…
options: baja la cuota mensual, pero cuesta más en total

cards.title: Los bancos captan y prestan

steps: El banco se queda el margen

cards.text: Los bancos reciben depósitos y prestan la mayor parte de ese dinero a tipos más altos. La diferencia, el margen de intereses, es una fuente clave de beneficios.

deep.x: Banks are intermediaries: they take deposits and borrow from markets, then lend to households and businesses at higher rates. The gap pays for costs and generates profit.
Maturity transformation
Banks borrow short-term (deposits you can withdraw any time) and lend long-term (30-year mortgages). This is useful for the economy but creates risk if depositors all want their money at once.
Sources of profit
When rates rise
Banks usually earn more as lending rates rise faster than deposit rates. Portuguese banks posted record profits in 2023 as Euribor jumped while deposit rates rose slowly.
A bank's business is managing the gap between what it pays and what it earns, and the risks that come with it.

cards.title: Creación de dinero
cards.text: Cuando un banco concede un préstamo, crea un nuevo depósito en la cuenta del prestatario. La mayor parte del dinero de la economía se crea así, con los límites de la regulación y la demanda.

deep.x: When a bank makes a loan, it doesn't hand out other people's savings. It creates a new deposit in the borrower's account. That's how most money in a modern economy comes into existence.
What limits it
Textbook vs reality
Why it matters

x: Credit booms expand the money supply and can fuel bubbles
Credit crunches shrink lending and slow the economy
Central banks influence money creation through interest rates, not by fixing quantities

deep.x: The Bank of England's 2014 paper "Money creation in the modern economy" helped make this mainstream understanding.

cards.title: Reserva fraccionaria
cards.text: Los bancos guardan solo una fracción de los depósitos como efectivo y reservas. Normalmente no pasa nada, pero si todos retiran a la vez, un pánico bancario puede hundirlo.

deep.x: Banks hold only a small fraction of deposits as cash or central bank reserves. The rest is tied up in loans and investments.
Why it normally works
On any given day, only a small share of depositors withdraw money, and new deposits come in. Banks also hold liquid assets they can sell or borrow against.
Liquidity rules
After 2008, the Basel III rules added the Liquidity Coverage Ratio: banks must hold enough high-quality liquid assets to survive 30 days of stressed outflows.
When it fails

steps: Bank sells assets at a loss

deep.x: The euro-area reserve requirement
Euro-area banks must hold 1% of certain deposits as minimum reserves at the central bank, a requirement in place since 2012.
Banks are safe in normal times because not everyone wants their money back at once.

cards.title: Garantía de depósitos
cards.text: En la UE, los depósitos están garantizados hasta 100 000 € por depositante y por banco. En Portugal, lo cubre el Fundo de Garantia de Depósitos.

deep.x: In the EU, bank deposits are protected up to €100,000 per depositor, per bank. If a bank fails, a deposit guarantee scheme pays back covered deposits.

items.l: working days to pay out (EU target)

deep.x: What's covered
Per bank, not per brand
Check whether two banks share one licence. If they do, the €100,000 limit applies once across both.
Joint accounts
Joint accounts are usually split equally among holders, so each holder is covered up to €100,000.
Lesson from Portugal
When Banco Espírito Santo collapsed in 2014, deposits were protected, but many retail investors lost money on commercial paper and bonds sold to them at bank branches, which were not deposits.

deep.w: All money at a bank is guaranteed
deep.r: only deposits are; investment products sold by banks are not

cards.title: Pánicos bancarios

steps: La alarma se propaga en redes
El banco vende activos con pérdidas

cards.text: En 2023, Silicon Valley Bank quebró después de que los depositantes retiraran 42 000 millones de dólares en un solo día, empujados por las redes sociales. La velocidad de los pánicos digitales es algo nuevo.

deep.x: A bank run happens when many depositors try to withdraw money at once, fearing the bank will fail. Even a healthy bank can be brought down because its money is tied up in loans.

events.l: Northern Rock queues in the UK

deep.x: Silicon Valley Bank

In March 2023, depositors withdrew about $42 billion from SVB in a single day, and requested more the next morning. Concerns about losses on its bond portfolio spread quickly on social media and messaging apps. Regulators closed it on 10 March.
Why runs are faster now
Defences

x: Deposit guarantees reduce the incentive to run
Central banks lend to solvent banks in a crisis
Liquidity rules require buffers
Resolution regimes allow orderly failure

deep.x: Runs are about confidence: guarantees work largely by making panic unnecessary.

cards.title: Requisitos de capital

items: Capital propio: absorbe primero las pérdidas

cards.text: Tras la crisis de 2008, los reguladores exigieron a los bancos tener más capital propio para absorber pérdidas, de modo que no tengan que hacerlo los contribuyentes.

deep.x: Capital is the bank's own money: shareholders' equity that absorbs losses before depositors or taxpayers are hurt. After 2008, regulators required much more of it.
Basel III

The international Basel III rules, agreed after the 2008 crisis, raised the quality and quantity of capital banks must hold and added a leverage ratio, a minimum of 3% capital against total exposures regardless of risk.
Why it matters

steps: Too little: bank fails or needs rescue

deep.x: Bail-in
EU rules since 2016 require losses to be borne by shareholders and certain creditors before public money is used. That's "bail-in" instead of "bail-out".

items: shareholders and creditors take losses first

deep.x: Portugal received a €78 billion international bailout in 2011, and the state spent billions supporting banks through the following decade.

cards.title: Márgenes y comisiones
cards.text: Los bancos también ganan con las comisiones: mantenimiento de cuenta, transferencias, tarjetas. Comparar comisiones puede ahorrarte decenas de euros al año; el Banco de Portugal publica comparativas.

Pay-as-you-go vs funded

Portugal's Social Security Financial Stabilisation Fund (FEFSS) holds reserves to support the system, managed separately from current payments.
A pay-as-you-go pension is a promise between generations.

cards.title: Una población que envejece
cards.text: Como vivimos más y tenemos menos hijos, hay menos trabajadores por pensionista, lo que presiona los sistemas de pensiones.

deep.x: Portugal has one of the oldest populations in the EU. People live longer and have fewer children, so there are fewer working-age people for each retiree.

deep.x: Why it's happening

x: Life expectancy at birth in Portugal is now about 81 years
Fertility around 1.4 children per woman, well below the 2.1 needed to replace the population
Emigration of young adults, especially during the 2011–2014 crisis

deep.x: Pressure on pensions
Responses
Immigration has boosted Portugal's population and social security contributions in recent years.

cards.title: El factor de sostenibilidad

steps: Se ajusta la edad de jubilación

cards.text: Portugal vincula la edad de jubilación a la esperanza de vida: a medida que vivimos más, la edad legal sube poco a poco y ya supera los 66 años.

deep.x: Portugal links pensions to life expectancy in two ways: the statutory retirement age rises as life expectancy at 65 increases, and a "sustainability factor" reduces pensions for those retiring early.
How the age is set
The normal retirement age is adjusted each year based on the change in life expectancy at 65. It can also fall if life expectancy falls, as happened briefly after COVID-19.
Early retirement

items: penalty per month early plus sustainability factor

deep.x: Long careers
People with very long contribution careers can retire earlier with reduced or no penalties under specific rules.
Check the latest
These parameters change annually. Segurança Social publishes the current normal retirement age and penalties each year.
Longer lives mean longer working lives, or smaller pensions.

cards.title: Tasa de sustitución

viz.f: tasa de sustitución = pensión ÷ último sueldo

cards.text: La tasa de sustitución es tu pensión como proporción de tu último sueldo. Las proyecciones apuntan a que los futuros jubilados en Portugal podrían recibir una proporción menor que los actuales.

deep.x: The replacement rate is your pension as a percentage of your earnings before retirement. It tells you how much your income drops when you stop working.

v.f: Replacement rate = first pension / final salary

deep.x: Trends
EU projections suggest that the average pension in Portugal will fall relative to average wages over the coming decades, as reforms and demographics take effect.
What it means for you

x: Expect state pension to cover less of your final salary
Plan extra savings to fill the gap
Lower earners typically get higher replacement rates

deep.x: How much do you need?
Check your projected pension early, while you still have time to close the gap.

cards.title: Tres pilares
cards.text: Los ingresos en la jubilación suelen apoyarse en tres pilares: la pensión pública, los planes de pensiones de empresa y el ahorro personal.

deep.x: Retirement income usually rests on three pillars. Relying on just one is risky.
In Portugal
Compared with countries like the Netherlands or Denmark, workplace pensions are relatively uncommon in Portugal, so personal savings matter more.
Diversifying

x: Different pillars carry different risks: political, employer, market
Combining them spreads risk
Property can be a pillar but is illiquid

deep.x: Workplace pension check

items: Can I take it with me?

deep.x: In some countries, workers are automatically enrolled in workplace pensions; the UK's 2012 auto-enrolment led to millions more people saving.

cards.title: Empieza pronto
cards.text: Gracias al interés compuesto, el dinero ahorrado entre los 20 y los 40 años tiene décadas para crecer. Ahorrar 100 € al mes desde los 25 puede superar a 200 € al mes desde los 45.

deep.x: Money saved early has decades to grow. Starting in your 20s or 30s can beat contributing much more later.
The power of time
Even small amounts

x: €50 a month at 25 is a strong start
Increase contributions with each raise
Automate so you don't have to think about it

deep.x: Catching up
Starting late is still far better than not starting. Save more, retire a little later or adjust expectations.
The best time to start was years ago; the second-best time is now.

cards.title: PPR

items: Rescate a la edad de jubilación o en casos especiales

cards.text: En Portugal, el Plano Poupança Reforma (PPR) es un producto de ahorro para la jubilación con ventajas fiscales sobre las aportaciones, dentro de unos límites, y con reglas sobre cuándo puedes retirar el dinero.

deep.x: The Plano Poupança Reforma (PPR) is a Portuguese retirement savings product with tax benefits. It can be a savings fund, an insurance product or an investment fund.
Tax benefit

items.b: deduction of 20% of contributions, up to €400

deep.x: Withdrawals

Without penalty: from age 60, or in specific situations such as long-term unemployment, serious illness, disability or, under certain conditions, to pay a home loan. Early withdrawals outside these cases may lose tax benefits.
Choosing a PPR

x: Compare fees: they compound over decades
Check past performance over long periods
Match risk to your age and horizon

deep.x: A PPR's tax benefit is a bonus; its fees and investments decide the result.

cards.title: La regla del 4 %
cards.text: Una pauta aproximada de estudios estadounidenses: retirar alrededor del 4 % de una cartera diversificada el primer año y luego ajustar por inflación ha durado históricamente unos 30 años. No es una garantía.

deep.x: The 4% rule comes from US studies in the 1990s by financial planner William Bengen and the "Trinity study". It estimates how much retirees can withdraw from savings without running out.
How it works
Withdraw 4% of your portfolio in year one, then the same amount adjusted for inflation each year. Historically, in US data, this lasted at least 30 years in almost all periods.
Caveats

x: Based on US stock and bond returns, which were unusually strong
Fees reduce what's sustainable
Retirements longer than 30 years need lower rates
Bad returns early in retirement are especially damaging

deep.x: The reverse

x: Need €20,000 a year from savings
= €500,000 target

deep.r: it's a historical rule of thumb, not a promise about the future

cards.title: La inflación en la jubilación
cards.text: En 25 años de jubilación, una inflación del 2 % reduce el poder adquisitivo de una pensión fija en torno a un 40 %. Unos ingresos que se ajusten a la inflación valen mucho.

deep.x: Retirement can last 25 years or more. Even moderate inflation over that time significantly reduces the buying power of a fixed income.

v.unit: buying power of €1,000 a month at 2% inflation, €

deep.x: Protection

items.b: updated annually by law, linked to inflation and growth

deep.x: Portuguese pension updates
Pensions are updated each year according to rules that consider inflation and economic growth, with lower pensions typically getting larger increases.
Plan for it

x: Keep some growth assets even in retirement
Don't assume today's costs will hold
Health costs often rise with age

deep.x: In a long retirement, inflation is a bigger risk than market swings.

cards.title: Revisa tu historial
cards.text: En Portugal, la web Segurança Social Direta muestra tu historial de cotizaciones y una simulación de pensión. Revisarlo pronto ayuda a planificar.

deep.x: Your pension depends on your contribution record. Checking it early lets you fix errors and plan.

steps: Log in to Segurança Social Direta

deep.x: What to check

items: Periods worked in other EU countries

deep.x: Working abroad
EU rules let contribution periods in different EU countries count together. Each country pays its share of your pension.
Errors
Employers sometimes declare wrong amounts or fail to pay contributions. Spotting this early makes correction easier.
Plan

items.b: what your own savings must cover

deep.x: A ten-minute check today can avoid unpleasant surprises at retirement.

cards.title: Alquilar o comprar
cards.text: Comprar genera patrimonio, pero inmoviliza dinero y conlleva costes como impuestos, mantenimiento e intereses. Alquilar da flexibilidad. La respuesta correcta depende de los precios, los tipos y cuánto tiempo vayas a quedarte.

deep.x: Whether to rent or buy depends on house prices, rents, interest rates, how long you'll stay and your other plans. Neither is always better.
Key factors
Break-even
Buying has high upfront costs (taxes, fees). Spread over few years, they make buying expensive. Staying longer, often five to seven years or more, usually favours buying.
The comparison

items.b: interest, IMI, condominium, insurance, maintenance, upfront taxes

deep.x: In Portugal

x: Home ownership is high: around three-quarters of households own their home
Rents in Lisbon and Porto rose sharply in the 2010s and 2020s
The rental market is small relative to demand

deep.x: Compare full costs over the time you expect to stay, not rent versus mortgage payment.

cards.title: La entrada
cards.text: Los bancos portugueses suelen prestar hasta el 90 % del valor de la vivienda habitual, así que necesitarás al menos un 10 % más los gastos. Una entrada mayor suele conseguir mejores diferenciales.

deep.x: Banks in Portugal typically lend up to 90% of the property's value for a primary home, under Banco de Portugal's macroprudential rules. You need at least 10% plus purchase costs.
Loan-to-value
Young buyer support
Since 2024, a state guarantee scheme lets eligible young buyers (35 or under) finance up to 100% of the price of a first home within limits, with the state guaranteeing part of the loan.
Bigger deposit, better terms

x: Lower loan-to-value often brings lower spreads
Smaller loan means lower payments
More buffer if prices fall

deep.x: Save for the deposit and the costs: the costs often surprise first-time buyers.

cards.title: Costes ocultos
cards.text: Además de la entrada, el comprador paga el impuesto de transmisión (IMT, con exenciones para algunos jóvenes y primeros compradores), el impuesto de timbre, el registro, la tasación y las comisiones bancarias.

deep.x: Beyond the deposit, buying a home in Portugal involves taxes, fees and charges that add up to several percent of the price.
Main taxes

items.b: progressive tax on transfer, varies by price and use

deep.x: Young buyer exemption
Since August 2024, people aged 35 or under buying their first permanent home are exempt from IMT and purchase stamp duty up to a price limit (around €316,000 in 2024), with partial relief above it.
Other costs

x: Bank valuation and processing fees
Life and home insurance required by the bank
Notary or Casa Pronta fees
Moving and furnishing
€250,000 home, no exemption
IMT ≈ several thousand € + stamp duty €2,000
+ loan stamp duty and fees

deep.x: Budget around 6–8% of the price for costs unless you qualify for exemptions.

cards.title: Cómo funciona la cuota hipotecaria
cards.text: Cada cuota mensual cubre los intereses más una parte del préstamo. Al principio, la mayor parte va a intereses; más adelante, la mayor parte va a devolver el préstamo.

deep.x: Most Portuguese mortgages use constant payments (if the rate doesn't change): each payment covers that month's interest plus some repayment of the loan. The mix shifts over time.
Example
Why
Interest is charged on the outstanding balance. Early on, the balance is large, so interest dominates. As it shrinks, more of each payment repays the loan.
Implication
Extra payments early in the loan save the most interest, because they reduce the balance on which decades of interest would be charged.
In the first years, you're mostly paying the bank for the use of its money.

cards.title: La cuota mensual
cards.text: Un préstamo de 200 000 € a 30 años al 4 % cuesta unos 955 € al mes. Al 3 %, unos 843 €. En 30 años, ese punto de diferencia suma unos 40 000 €.

deep.x: Interest rates have a big effect on both monthly payments and total cost over a 30-year mortgage.
Total interest
The formula
Term matters too
A one-point difference in rate is worth negotiating hard for.

deep.x: Portuguese mortgages have traditionally been variable-rate, tied to Euribor. Fixed and mixed rates have become more popular since the 2022–23 rate shock.

Mixed loans fix the rate for an initial period (often 2–10 years), then switch to variable. They offer temporary certainty.

budget is tight and certainty matters

deep.x: Before borrowing, check whether you could still pay if rates rose 2–3 percentage points. Banks do this; you should too.
2023's lesson
Many families with variable-rate mortgages saw payments jump by €200–400 a month within a year as Euribor rose from below zero to over 4%.
Your own test
Building resilience

x: Keep an emergency fund covering several months of payments
Don't borrow the maximum the bank offers
Consider fixing part or all of the rate

deep.x: If a rate rise would break your budget, the loan is too big.

cards.title: Amortización anticipada

cards.text: La vivienda en las ciudades portuguesas se ha encarecido mucho en relación con los ingresos locales. Compara el precio de la casa con los ingresos anuales del hogar para valorar si es asequible.

deep.x: Price-to-income compares house prices with annual household income. It's a simple measure of affordability.

v.f: Price-to-income = house price / annual household income

deep.x: Rough benchmarks
Portugal's affordability problem
House prices in Portugal more than doubled between 2015 and 2024 while incomes grew much more slowly. Lisbon, Porto and the Algarve are among the least affordable areas relative to local incomes.
Drivers
Policy responses

x: Programmes to increase public and affordable housing
Tax incentives for young buyers
Changes to rules for short-term rentals

deep.x: The OECD and IMF have repeatedly flagged Portugal's house prices as high relative to incomes.

cards.title: Coste total de ser propietario
cards.text: Suma los intereses de la hipoteca, el IMI (impuesto sobre la propiedad), la comunidad, el seguro y el mantenimiento (a menudo ~1 % del valor al año) antes de comparar con el alquiler.

deep.x: Owning a home costs much more than the mortgage payment. Adding everything up gives a fair comparison with renting.
Typical yearly costs on a €250,000 flat
IMI
Municipal property tax (IMI) is charged annually at 0.3–0.45% of the property's tax value (VPT), which is often lower than market value. Municipalities set the rate.
Maintenance
A common rule of thumb is about 1% of the property's value a year on average, more for older buildings.
Compare fairly
Owning isn't "paying yourself": interest, taxes and upkeep are real costs too.
